title: Low-Rank Spectral Flow Matching for Human Trajectory Prediction

problem.claim: Human trajectory prediction must model the multimodal conditional distribution of future coordinates.

gap.claim: Existing generative models do not distinguish which trajectory dimensions require diverse prediction because spatiotemporal diversity is entangled across timesteps.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes Low-Rank Spectral Flow Matching, which performs conditional flow matching in truncated DCT space instead of raw coordinate space.
The paper introduces Spectral Diversity Loss with learnable per-mode margins to identify spectral modes requiring diverse predictions.
The paper analyzes diversity and trajectory energy across DCT spectral modes, identifying concentrated diversity and low-rank energy structure.

author_reported_evidence.claim: FDR values for specific spectral components are reported as 20–600 times higher than for others.
More than 99% of trajectory energy is reported as retained empirically in a few low-frequency DCT modes.
Experiments on ETH–UCY, SDD, and NBA are reported to achieve state-of-the-art performance across multiple evaluation metrics.

narrative_sequence.summary: Human trajectory prediction involves multimodal future-coordinate distributions.
Existing models struggle to identify which trajectory dimensions require diverse prediction.
Diversity and energy are concentrated in a small number of DCT spectral modes.
The proposed approach performs flow matching in truncated DCT space and learns per-mode diversity margins.
The method is evaluated on three trajectory-prediction datasets with multiple metrics.

unknowns: Exact evaluation metrics, baselines, and numerical results are not supplied.
